pNone_chapter_1: Byomkesh Bakshi and Ajit stand at the edge of a dense, sun-dappled forest in Baghmari, with the metallic lines of a railway track visible in the distance. Byomkesh, dressed in a crisp white dhoti-kurta and a light shawl, stands with a contemplative expression, holding a smoldering cigarette as he surveys the surrounding paddy fields. Beside him, the slightly stockier Ajit observes the old, weathered stone architecture of a nearby village house with a paved courtyard. The late afternoon light casts long, sharp shadows across the rural landscape, highlighting the contrast between the lush greenery and the rusted barbed-wire fencing of the railway line. The atmosphere is quiet and observant, capturing the two men as they begin their investigation in the rural Bengal setting.
